messages.content:
Sarunyu has a stick of length 1 with one endpoint marked in red. Every minute, he picks one of his sticks uniformly at random and breaks it into two halves of equal length. Compute the expected length of the stick with the red endpoint after 5 minutes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
After each break, the total number of sticks increases by 1, so just before minute \(t\) there are \(t\) sticks.

Exactly one stick contains the red endpoint at all times. Therefore, at minute \(t\), the probability he picks the red stick is

\[
\frac{1}{t}.
\]

If he picks the red stick, its length is multiplied by \(\frac12\). If he does not, its length is unchanged. So the expected multiplier for minute \(t\) is

\[
\frac12\cdot \frac12+\frac{t-1}{t}\cdot 1
=1-\frac{1}{2t}.
\]

Thus the expected length after 5 minutes is

\[
\prod_{t=1}^{5}\left(1-\frac{1}{2t}\right)
=
\frac12\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac56\cdot\frac78\cdot\frac9{10}.
\]

Computing,

\[
\frac{1\cdot 3\cdot 5\cdot 7\cdot 9}{2\cdot 4\cdot 6\cdot 8\cdot 10}
=
\frac{945}{3840}
=
\frac{63}{256}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{63}{256}}
\]
